senses.definition: tell or ask someone to do something
be called; have a particular name
call out; speak loudly to attract attention

examples.sentence: 刘焉发布招军榜，叫人到处报名。
两队人在山下相遇，刘备叫黄巾军投降。
皇帝信任张让，叫他“阿父”，朝政逐渐败坏，天下人心想要作乱，盗贼纷纷起来。
大汉叫张飞，住在涿郡，有田，卖酒杀猪，也喜爱结交豪杰。
那人叫关羽，曾因杀了当地一个仗势欺人的人，逃难了五六年。
他大声骂敌人背叛汉朝，叫他们早些投降。
他又让人传出“苍天已死，黄天当立”和“岁在甲子，天下大吉”的话，叫百姓在家门上写“甲子”。
正饮酒时，一个大汉推着一辆车来到店门前休息，进门便叫酒保斟酒，说要赶进城投军。
张角让手下向百姓传话，说旧的天下已经衰弱，新的天下将要出现，还叫人用白土在家门上写下“甲子”二字。
正饮之间，一个大汉推车到店门口歇下，入店便叫酒保倒酒，说要赶进城投军。

previous.explanation_en: 叫 is a verb that can direct someone to do something, as in 叫他走 (“tell him to go”). With a person followed by a name, it says what that person is called, as in 他叫李明 (“he is called Li Ming”).

parts.contribution_en: The verb directs someone toward an action, or predicates the name by which someone is called; what follows determines the use.

sources.title: 现代汉语词典（第七版）
sources.summary_en: The entry separates a use meaning ‘make; command’ (with an example 叫他早点回去) from a use meaning ‘is; is called’ (with 我叫王勇). The page supports the target senses, though it is a third-party-hosted dictionary entry.

sources.title: 教育部《國語辭典簡編本》2021: 叫
sources.summary_en: The Ministry of Education dictionary lists 叫 as ‘be named/called,’ as summoning or calling someone (often with a commanding tone), and as ‘make, let, cause.’ Its examples distinguish these uses.

sources.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 叫
sources.summary_en: The entry gives the Shuowen gloss 嘑也 and cites early examples of calling or shouting, a Han example of calling a friend, and later examples of naming and passive 叫. It documents these senses and examples but does not demonstrate that the modern target senses developed from the older vocal-call sense.

sources.title: 叫 jiào - 汉典
sources.summary_en: The entry lists ‘name/be called’ and ‘make, command’ among modern senses, and reproduces the Shuowen gloss 嘑也. The classical examples shown primarily illustrate vocal calling or shouting; they do not establish a historical derivation of the target uses.

sources.title: 近代汉语使役动词及其相关的句法、语义结构
sources.summary_en: The journal article abstract says causative 叫-constructions came into use in the Ming-Qing period and that 叫, unlike 使/令/遣, took a less direct path to causative use. It describes causative verbs becoming semantically bleached in serial-verb constructions, but the abstract does not specify a path from the vocal-call sense of 叫.

sources.title: 汉语使役句句法、语义的历时研究
sources.summary_en: The dissertation abstract describes causative constructions developing through reanalysis of verbs in the first position of serial-verb constructions, and says the 叫 construction historically replaced the 教 construction. It attributes variation in their development to multiple factors. This supports a proposed history for causative 叫, but not a derivation from the older sense ‘call/shout’.

claims.text_en: In the example 刘焉发布招军榜，叫人到处报名, 叫 relates 人 to the following action: someone is told or directed to register in various places. This fits the dictionary use glossed as ‘make; command’ and the Ministry dictionary’s command-toned calling/summoning use. The sentence does not specify whether the directive is polite or coercive.

In 那人说自己叫关羽, 叫 predicates the name by which the person says he is called: the person’s name is Guan Yu. The naming dictionaries and their examples support this use; they do not specify who assigned the name or whether it is formal.

The consulted character references report an older vocal-call or shout sense: the Shuowen gloss is 嘑也, and cited early texts use 叫 for calling or shouting. Those attestations establish an older sense, but do not by themselves prove that either the modern directive use or the naming use derives from it.

A historical account of causative constructions places causative 叫 in the Ming-Qing period and describes it as developing through grammatical reanalysis; a dissertation abstract additionally characterizes 叫 as replacing the causative 教 construction. These accounts support a history for the causative construction, but do not establish that it arose specifically from the ancient vocal-call sense or explain the historical development of the naming predicate.

gaps: The opened references attest the old vocal-call sense and the modern naming use, but do not show when or through what intermediate contexts 叫 developed its ‘be called/name’ use. The causative histories consulted describe grammatical reanalysis and/or replacement of 教, but the available abstracts do not establish a derivation from the vocal-call sense or provide a detailed lexical pathway for the target directive construction.
